title: Game Character Costume Design with AI: The Concept-Art Workflow
lede: How concept artists actually use AI for costume design — from mood board to palette sheet to final render, with the three-level reference ladder that keeps you copyright-safe.
body_md:
## The professional workflow
Mood board (10 refs) → palette sheet (3 colors + accent) → silhouette sketch → AI generation for variants → hand-polish. AI sits at the variants stage: it multiplies your iterations, not replaces your eye.

## Prompt skeleton for costume concepts
Base: 'fantasy character design, concept art, official art style, painterly rendering'. Then per-layer: silhouette words → fabric words → palette sentence → prop words.

## The three-level reference ladder
L1 Palette only (commercial-safe) → L2 Silhouette borrowing (fan-art convention) → L3 Frame recreation (personal appreciation, label as fan art). Most 'inspired by' posts online are actually L2 without credit — credit yours.

## Where AI fails in costume design
Symmetry enforcement, consistent fastenings across angles, and cultural garment rules (collar directions, layering order). Fix these in hand-polish, or constrain with explicit words.
faq: Do I need to draw to use AI for costume design?
No — but you need vocabulary. Our fabric, lighting and palette guides give you the words that replace drawing skills at the concept stage.
